subject: SIG mapping & subprocessor risk heatmap for Arcadia Labs integration
messages:
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@arcadia-labs.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Arcadia Labs Security <security@arcadia-labs.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: SIG mapping + subprocessor risk heatmap for our onboarding

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist at Arcadia Labs, our security team has a couple of deliverables we need before we finalize the integration: a SIG control-to-evidence mapping and a subprocessor risk heatmap that highlights custody of keys, data residency, and any transitive subprocessors.

I attached our template (Arcadia_SIG_Questions.xlsx) — can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: 
- A completed SIG mapping (control -> artifact / doc / log)
- A subprocessor roster with a simple risk rating (Low/Med/High) and whether they have KMS access or key custody
- Notes on any on-prem or regionally-hosted components that could affect residency controls

Can you share an estimated delivery date? We have a gated procurement window and ideally need the artifacts by the end of next week. If there are items you need from us (e.g., precise dataflows or contract clauses), let me know and I can loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Paul Nguyen
Director, InfoSec
Arcadia Labs

Attachment: Arcadia_SIG_Questions.xlsx

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@arcadia-labs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG mapping + subprocessor risk heatmap for our onboarding

Paul — thanks for the clear ask and the template. We're glad Arcadia is prioritizing this.

Quick responses and proposed plan:
- We can produce a SIG control mapping document tied to artifacts we maintain (policies, SOC 2 reports, access logs, KMS attestations). Expect a draft in 5 business days.
- We will deliver a subprocessor roster + risk heatmap. We'll include a "key custody" column and a brief note for each subprocessor (e.g., KMS provider, ephemeral key usage, agent/contractor access).

Questions we have to make the deliverable accurate:
1) For residency, do you need location of compute (GPUs), storage (S3 buckets), or both called out separately?
2) Do you want us to flag any subprocessor that handles ephemeral telemetry (metrics/traces) vs. persisted customer data?

Action items from Redwood (proposed timeline):
- Today: acknowledge and kick off internal inventory (this email) — attachment: request_acknowledgement.pdf
- +2 business days: internal subprocessor inventory + preliminary heatmap
- +5 business days: SIG control mapping draft + evidence index

If that works, Ben and Marissa will coordinate the inventory and evidence collection. We will upload the draft artifacts to the shared Drive link below and send the HubSpot ticked for tracking.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_drive_link
HubSpot: HS-1234567

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: request_acknowledgement.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@arcadia-labs.com>
Date: 2027-02-12T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG mapping + subprocessor risk heatmap for our onboarding

Grace / Marissa / Paul — jumping in with the first-pass inventory. Quoting Paul's original ask below.

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 9:12 AM Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@arcadia-labs.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our procurement checklist at Arcadia Labs, our security team has a couple of deliverables we need before we finalize the integration: a SIG control-to-evidence mapping and a subprocessor risk heatmap that highlights custody of keys, data residency, and any transitive subprocessors.

Preliminary subprocessor roster (first-pass):
- Cloud infra: AWS (compute/storage) — Risk: Low/Med depending on account separation. Data residency: multi-region; primary us-west-2. KMS ownership: Redwood-managed CMKs (custody retained by Redwood), customer-managed CMK optional for Private deployments.
- GPU provider: LambdaCompute (managed GPU fleet) — Risk: Med (hardware access, telemetry). KMS: no direct key custody; uses provider-managed encryption at rest.
- Monitoring/telemetry: Tracelytics — Risk: Low (metrics only) — ephemeral telemetry only, no PII.
- Embedding index provider (optional): VectorStoreX — Risk: Med/High (if used for persisted vector storage) — supports customer-managed encryption keys in Dedicated/Private setups.
- Payroll / HR (vendor contact for procurement): ProcureCorp — Risk: Low (not in data path).

Notes / open items:
- Need to confirm whether Arcadia wants explicit flagging for any subprocessor that could access raw prompts during troubleshooting (we do redaction by default but engineers sometimes request limited logs).
- I'll attach the CSV inventory and a short KMS roster. These are internal working artifacts — we'll sanitize before the SIG mapping handoff.

Attachments: subproc_inventory_20270212.csv, kms_roster.txt

Ben
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@arcadia-labs.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Arcadia Labs Security <security@arcadia-labs.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T14:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: SIG mapping + subprocessor risk heatmap for our onboarding

Grace / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the inventory snapshot. The roster looks good. A couple of clarifications before we consider the deliverables complete: 

- Please flag any subprocessor with potential access to unredacted prompts (even if it is "on request" during troubleshooting) — that will affect our classification.
- For VectorStoreX: if it is optional in Dedicated flows, please include the control that documents its encryption-at-rest configuration and whether customer-managed keys are supported.
- Please upload the sanitized CSV and the draft SIG mapping to the Drive folder and update HS-1234567 when done so our procurement team can pick it up.

If you can get the draft uploaded by EOD Wednesday 2027-02-18, that should keep us on schedule. Appreciate the coordination — Carmen from ProcureCorp will start our internal review once artifacts are in Drive.

Thanks,
Paul
Director, InfoSec
Arcadia Labs

Quoted from Ben's message above for context.
